Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:11:1.english: And how much - is considered scattered?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:11:2.hebrew: קב - מפוזר בארבע אמות, אבל בג' אמות לא הוי פיזור, וטעמא מפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:11:2.english: A kav - [That is] scattered over four cubits, but in three cubits it is not [considered] scattered, and [the Gemara] proceeds to explain the reason.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:12:1.hebrew: אי דרך נפילה - אם מצאם דרך נפילה, שיש לדעת שלא הונחו שם מדעת אלא נפלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:12:1.english: If [in] a manner of falling - If he found them [in] a manner of falling, such that one can know that they were not placed there intentionally, but rather fell.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:12:2.hebrew: אפילו טובא - מקב נמי, דכיון דאין בהן סימן, איאושי מיאש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:12:2.english: Even more - [than] a kav as well [belongs to the finder], for since there is no distinguishing mark on them, [the owner] certainly despairs [of recovering them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:12:3.english: And if [it was in] a manner of placement, etc. - [The owner] will return in the future and take them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:13:1.hebrew: במכנשתא דבי דרי - בשעת אסיפת גרנות, וכאן דשן בעליהן ונשאו את העיקר, ונותרו אלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:13:1.english: With the gathering of the threshing floor - At the time of gathering the threshing floors, and here their owners threshed them and carried away the main [portion], and these remained.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:13:2.english: Their exertion is great - To gather them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:13:3.english: Less than this - If their scattering was in less than this [area].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:14:1.english: Because they are not significant - [That is,] a kav of produce [is not significant] to him to exert [himself] over them [with] the effort of gathering [across] four cubits.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:16:1.hebrew: שומשמין - דקין מאד, ויש טורח בקיבוצן יותר מחטין, אבל דמיהן יקרין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:16:1.english: Sesame [seeds] - [They are] very small, and there is more exertion in gathering them than [with] wheat, but their value is high.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:17:1.hebrew: תמרים ורמונין - גסים הן, ואין טורח בקבוצן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:17:1.english: Dates and pomegranates - They are large, and there is no trouble in gathering them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:1:1.hebrew: דשיילינן להו - אם ראו הפרעון, ואם לאו, נאמן המלוה לומר שלא נכתב אלא להיות מוכן לכשיפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:1:1.english: As we ask them - Whether they saw the repayment; and if not, the lender is believed to say that it was only written to be ready for when he would be repaid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:2:1.hebrew: עדי קיום - שכתבו הנפק, דבי דינא לא מקיימי ליה אלא א"כ פרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:2:1.english: Witnesses of ratification - Who wrote a court ratification [henpek], for the court does not ratify it unless [the debtor] paid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:1.english: A simpon upon which witnesses [are signed] - We establish it [as referring to] witnesses of ratification.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:2.hebrew: יתקיים בחותמיו - ואפי' יוצא מתחת יד מלוה, כשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:2.english: It is ratified by its signatories - And even [if] it emerges from the possession of [the] lender, [it is] valid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:3.english: There are no witnesses of ratification on it - but witnesses are signed on it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:4.hebrew: ויוצא מתחת ידי שליש - שאין הלוה מוציאו ולא המלוה, אלא שליש שביניהם נאמן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:4.english: And [it] emerges from the possession of a third party - For neither the borrower nor the lender produces it, rather the third party between them [is] trustworthy.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:5.hebrew: או שיצא אחר חיתום שטרות - שיצא לפנינו כשהוא כתוב בשטר חוב אחר החתימה, כשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:4:5.english: Or if it emerges after the signing of documents - [Meaning] that it came out before us while written in a promissory note after the signature; [it is] valid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:5:1.english: For the creditor trusted the third party - For perforce, only the creditor writes a receipt, and he handed it over into the possession of the third party.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:1.hebrew: אלו מציאות: מצא פירות מפוזרין - נתייאשו הבעלים מהן, כדאמר בגמרא, והפקר הן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:1.english: These found items [belong to him]: [if one] found scattered produce - The owners have despaired of [recovering] them, as stated in the Gemara, and they are ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:2.hebrew: מעות מפוזרות - הואיל ואין להם סימן ניכר, איאושי מיאש והוו להו הפקר. וזהו טעם כולם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:2.english: Scattered coins - Since they have no recognizable mark, [the owner] despairs [of recovering them] and they become ownerless [property]. And this is the reason for all of them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:3.hebrew: כריכות - עומרים קטנים, כמו מאלמים אלומים, ומתרגמינן בירושל' מכרכן כריכן (בראשית ל״ז:ז׳):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:3.english: Bundles - Small sheaves, as in [the verse] "binding sheaves" (Genesis 37:7), which we translate in [Targum] Yerushalmi as "mekharkhan kerikhan" [binding bundles].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:4.hebrew: ברה"ר - שהכל דשין עלייהו, ואם היה סימן נקשר עליהן, הרי הוא נשחת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:4.english: In a public domain - For everyone treads upon them, and if a [distinguishing] mark was tied onto them, it is ruined.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:5.hebrew: של נחתום - כל ככרות הנחתומין שוין, אבל ככרות של בעל הבית יש בהן סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:5.english: Of a baker - All bakers' loaves are alike, whereas the loaves of a householder have a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:6.hebrew: ממדינתן - כמות שהן גזוזות, כשאר כל גיזת המדינה, לאפוקי הבאות מבית האומן, כדקתני סיפא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:6.english: From their state [of origin] - Just as they are shorn, like all other shearings of the region, excluding those coming from the craftsman's house, as the latter clause teaches.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:7.hebrew: אניצי פשתן - רישט"א בל' אשכנז, ובמקומינו פופי"ר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:7.english: Flax stalks - [Called] rista in the language of Ashkenaz [German], and in our region popir [Old French: a bundle of combed flax].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:8.hebrew: ולשון של ארגמן - צמר סרוק ומשוך כמין לשון, וצבוע ארגמן, ומצויין הן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:8:8.english: And a tongue of purple wool - Combed wool, drawn out like a tongue, and dyed purple; and they are common.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 21a:9:1.english: He found a round [cake] - Of pressed figs.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:11:1.hebrew: וכמה א"ר יצחק קב בארבע אמות - צריך לומר דרבי יצחק גופיה בעי "וכמה", דאי גמרא בעי, מאי בעי "וכמה"? לוקי דרך נפילה ואפילו טובא, כדפריך גמ' בתר הכי. אלא מדברי רבי יצחק הוא, ורבי יצחק לא בעי לאוקמי דרך נפילה ואפילו טובא, משום דסבר כאביי דיאוש שלא מדעת לא הוי יאוש, אלא מוקי לה במכנשתא דבי דרי שהניחם שם מדעת. וכה"ג איכא בפירקין (דף ל:), דבעי: "ולעולם? אמר רב יהודה" כו', דצריך לומר דרב יהודה אמר "ולעולם". וכן בפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כב: ושם ד"ה וכמה) גבי מרחיקין מן החלונות, דקאמר: "וכמה? אמר רב ייבא: כמלוא רוחב חלון":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:11:1.english: And how much? Rabbi Yitzḥak said: A kav in four cubits - It is necessary to say that Rabbi Yitzḥak himself asked "And how much?", for if the Gemara asked [it], why did it ask "And how much?"? Let it establish [the Mishnah as referring to produce scattered in] the manner of falling, and even a large amount, as the Gemara objects afterwards. Rather, [the question] is part of Rabbi Yitzḥak's words, and Rabbi Yitzḥak does not want to establish [the Mishnah as referring to] the manner of falling and even a large amount, because he holds like Abaye that unconscious abandonment is not [valid] abandonment; rather, he establishes it as referring to the sweepings of the threshing floor, which [the owner] left there intentionally. And similar to this there is in our chapter (30b), where it asks: "And forever? Rav Yehudah said" etc., where it is necessary to say that Rav Yehudah said "And forever." And similarly in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yaḥpor (Bava Batra 22b, and there s.v. Vechamah) regarding "one must distance [a ladder] from the windows," where it says: "And how much? Rav Yeiva said: The full width of a window."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:14:1.hebrew: חצי קב בשתי אמות מהו - תימה: הלא קב בארבע אמות הוי נמי חצי קב בשתי אמות, ומאי קמבעיא ליה? וי"ל: כיון דליכא אלא חצי קב — ילקוט, כיון שאין לו טורח לגמור; אבל קב בארבע אמות — יש לו טורח ללקוט הכל, ואין מלקט כלל. אי נמי: קב בארבע אמות מרובעין הוי חצי קב בשתי אמות רוחב וארבע אמות אורך, והכא בעי חצי קב בב' אמות על ב' אמות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:14:1.english: "A half-kav in two cubits, what is [the halakha]?" - [This is] astonishing! Is not a kav in four cubits also a half-kav in two cubits, so what is [Rabbi Yirmeya] asking? And one can answer: Since there is only a half-kav, he will gather [it], because he does not have the exertion of finishing [a full kav]; whereas [with] a kav in four cubits, he has the exertion of gathering all of it, and he does not gather [it] at all. Alternatively: A kav in four square cubits is [equivalent to] a half-kav in two cubits width and four cubits length, whereas here he asks [about] a half-kav in two cubits by two cubits.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:8:1.hebrew: אלו מציאות שלו: כריכות ברה"ר - בכריכות דוקא מפליג בין רה"ר לרה"י, משום דלמ"ד (לקמן בבא מציעא כב:) סימן העשוי לידרס הוי סימן ומקום הוי סימן — מיירי הכא דליכא סימן, ומקום נמי לא הוי סימן ברה"ר משום דמנשתפי, וברה"י הוי מקום סימן וחייב להכריז, ומיירי דאשכח דרך הינוח. וככרות של נחתום ועיגולי דבילה אין בהם סימן, והוי שלו אף ברה"י, ומיירי דמצא דרך נפילה, ולכך לא הוי מקום סימן. וא"ת: אמאי נקט כריכות דאשכח דרך הינוח טפי משאר דאיירי דרך נפילה? וי"ל: דכריכות, איידי דיקירי אינון, לא הוה שיפלו שלא מדעת, אלא כשעומד לפוש מניח לארץ ושכחם שם. וככרות של בעה"ב יש להן סימן, דבעלי בתים רגילים לעשות סימן בככרותיהן, ולכך אפילו ברשות הרבים חייב להכריז, דסימן העשוי לידרס הוי סימן. וציבורי מעות ופירות דהוי מקום סימן אף ברה"ר כדאמר לקמן — משום דלא שייך בהו מנשתפי. ואם תאמר: כריכות ברה"ר דמיירי דרך הינוח, היאך לוקחם? הא אמרינן לקמן "ספק הינוח לא יטול", וכל שכן ודאי הינוח! וי"ל: דה"מ כשמצא במקום מוצנע ומשתמר, דלא יטול אם אין בו סימן, ואם יש בו סימן נוטל ומכריז. ולמ"ד (לקמן בבא מציעא כב:) סימן העשוי לידרס לא הוי סימן ומקום נמי לא הוי סימן — מיירי בכריכות שיש בהם סימן, ולכך ברה"י מכריז. וככרות של נחתום ושאר דמתניתין לית בהו סימן, ולכך אף ברה"י הם שלו. וככרות של בעה"ב שיש בהם סימן חייב להכריז אף ברה"ר, דאין עשוי לידרס, משום דאין מעבירין על האוכלין. וכולה מתני' מיירי בין דרך נפילה בין דרך הינוח. וא"ת: כריכות אי דרך נפילה היא, אם כן אינו יודע היכן נפלו, וברשות היחיד אמאי צריך להכריז? הא מתייאש, שסבור ברה"ר נפיל! וי"ל: דאע"פ שאינו יודע לכוין המקום, יודע הוא אם נפל ברשות הרבים או ברשות היחיד:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21a:8:1.english: These found items belong to him: bundles in a public domain - It specifically distinguishes between a public domain and a private domain with regard to bundles, because according to the one who says (later, Bava Metzia 22b) that an identifying mark that is prone to be trampled is a valid identifying mark and that location is a valid identifying mark — [our Mishnah] here is speaking of [bundles] that have no identifying mark; and location is also not an identifying mark in a public domain because they get kicked around, whereas in a private domain location is an identifying mark and one is obligated to proclaim [the find], and [the Mishnah] is speaking of where he found [them placed] in the manner of intentional placement. Whereas baker's loaves and round cakes of pressed figs have no identifying mark, so they are his even in a private domain, as [the Mishnah] is speaking of where he found [them] in the manner of having been dropped, and therefore location is not an identifying mark. And if you ask: Why did [the Mishnah] state [the case of] bundles as [found] in the manner of intentional placement rather than the other [items], which speak of [being found] in the manner of having been dropped? One can answer: Because bundles are heavy, they would not fall without [the owner's] awareness; rather, when he stops to rest, he sets them down on the ground and forgets them there. And homeowner's loaves have an identifying mark, for homeowners are accustomed to make an identifying mark on their loaves; therefore, even in a public domain one is obligated to proclaim [them], since an identifying mark that is prone to be trampled is a valid identifying mark. And [the reason] that [for] piles of coins and produce, location is an identifying mark even in a public domain, as [the Gemara] says later, is because getting kicked around does not apply to them. And if you ask: Bundles in a public domain, which [the Mishnah] discusses [as found] in the manner of intentional placement — how may [the finder] take them? Surely we say later [that in a case of] uncertain placement one may not take [it], and all the more so [in a case of] certain placement! One can answer: That applies when one finds [it] in a hidden and guarded place, where one may not take [it] if it has no identifying mark, and if it has an identifying mark one takes [it] and proclaims [it]. And according to the one who says (later, Bava Metzia 22b) that an identifying mark that is prone to be trampled is not a valid identifying mark, and location is also not a valid identifying mark — [the Mishnah] is speaking of bundles that have an identifying mark, and therefore in a private domain he proclaims [them]. Whereas baker's loaves and the rest of [the items in] our Mishnah have no identifying mark, and therefore even in a private domain they are his. And homeowner's loaves, which have an identifying mark, one is obligated to proclaim even in a public domain, because they are not prone to be trampled, since one does not pass over food [without picking it up]. And the entire Mishnah speaks both of [finding] in the manner of having been dropped and of [finding] in the manner of intentional placement. And if you ask: [Regarding] bundles, if it is in the manner of having been dropped, then [the owner] does not know where they fell, so in a private domain why must [the finder] proclaim [them]? Surely [the owner] despairs [of recovering them], as he assumes they fell in a public domain! One can answer: Even though he does not know how to pinpoint the exact spot, he knows whether it fell in a public domain or in a private domain.
